title: The End of Apps — Kitze, Sizzy.co
talk_summary: He demos his own 'Wolfer' tool whose main transferable idea is replacing agent memory with a nested-topic hierarchy that injects parent-topic descriptions into the first prompt.

takeaways.technique: Nested-topic context injection instead of memory retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: Organizes work into a tree of topics (work > projects > Benji > customer support); when a conversation starts in a leaf topic, the system concatenates the descriptions of all ancestor topics into the first prompt so the agent knows scope without a retrieval/memory system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it just looks at the topic, the parent topic, the parent topic, the parent topic. It takes all the descriptions together and it immediately knows

takeaways.technique: Purpose-scoped agents with visible model/capability config
takeaways.what_they_do: Each bot is contained to one purpose with its own model, system prompt/soul, tool list, and permissions; the UI shows which agent/model/capabilities are active in a conversation and lets you toggle capabilities off.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I tried to like contain every bot to have a purpose in my life

takeaways.technique: Cron messages labeled and grounded in full conversation
takeaways.what_they_do: Scheduled (cron) messages are tagged as cron and the agent reads the entire conversation context when handling them, so it doesn't act confused about where the trigger came from.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you get a cron message, it actually reads from the entire conversation and it labels it as cron

takeaways.technique: Invert prompting: agent drives the human with next-task queue
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues the productive pattern is agents continuously working in the background and prompting the human for decisions/inputs (forms, questionnaires) rather than humans prompting agents each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the fully productive people will be the one who delegate 99% of the stuff for to the AI and then the AI prompts you

takeaways.what_they_do: Rejects the premise that memory systems reliably pull the right context, preferring deterministic structural context (topic hierarchy) over retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't believe in memory of agents
